facts.statement: The only known species, A. lymense, was discovered in Early Jurassic rocks at Lyme Regis in the United Kingdom.
facts.quote: It is known from a single type species, A. lymense, discovered in Early Jurassic rocks of Lyme Regis in the United Kingdom.

facts.statement: The animal is known only from holotype NHMUK OR 49202, a complete skull, palate, mandible, and eight associated cervical vertebrae.
facts.quote: Anningasaura is known only from the holotype specimen NHMUK OR 49202, which consists of a complete skull, palate, and mandible, with eight associated cervical vertebrae, including the atlas-axis complex.

facts.statement: The fossil material represents a juvenile plesiosaur.
facts.quote: The partial skeleton came from a juvenile plesiosaur.

facts.statement: The specimen was collected from Hettangian to early Sinemurian-aged beds of the Lower Lias Group at Lyme Regis, Dorset.
facts.quote: NHMUK OR 49202 was collected at Lyme Regis, of Dorset, from the Hettangian to early Sinemurian-aged beds of the Lower Lias Group.

facts.statement: The skull possesses several unique features not seen in other plesiosaurians.
facts.quote: It also shows several autapomorphies not observed in other plesiosaurians.

facts.statement: The posteromedial processes of the premaxillae form a dorsoventrally thick, mediolaterally expanded platform, and the cultriform process of the parasphenoid is wider than the combined posterior interpterygoid vacuities.
facts.quote: Its posteromedial processes of the premaxillae (or possible anterior portion of the frontal) forming a dorsoventrally thick, mediolaterally expanded platform and its cultriform process of the parasphenoid is wider mediolaterally than the combined posterior interpterygoid vacuities.

facts.statement: The skull has two closely spaced foramina on the lateral surface of the exoccipital.
facts.quote: It also has two closely spaced foramina in the lateral surface of the exoccipital.

facts.statement: Unique features include a supplementary foramen penetrating the parietal sagittal crest, no contact between the pterygoid and vomer, and no contact between the pterygoids in the palate.
facts.quote: Additional autapomorphies are the presence of supplementary foramen penetrating the parietal sagittal crest, the absence of a pterygoid-vomerine contact and the absence of a contact between the pterygoids in palatal aspect.

facts.statement: Phylogenetic analysis places Anningasaura as a basal, non-neoplesiosaurian plesiosaur.
facts.quote: A phylogenetic analysis performed by Benson et al. (2012) found it to be a basal, non-neoplesiosaurian, plesiosaur.

facts.statement: Peggy Vincent and Roger B. J. Benson named the genus and its type species in 2012.
facts.quote: Anningasaura was first described and named by Peggy Vincent and Roger B. J. Benson in 2012 and the type species is Anningasaura lymense.

facts.statement: The genus name honors Mary Anning, a famous British fossil collector from Lyme Regis.
facts.quote: The generic name honors Mary Anning, a British fossil collector who became known around the world for finds she made in the Jurassic marine fossil beds at Lyme Regis in Dorset.

facts.statement: The species name is derived from the Lyme Regis locality where the specimen was found.
facts.quote: The specific name is derived from the name of the Lyme Regis locality where the only known specimen was collected.

facts.statement: Anningasaura belongs to the order Plesiosauria.
A phylogenetic analysis by Benson et al. (2012) determined it was a basal non-neoplesiosaurian plesiosaur.
facts.quote: Un análisis filogenético desarrollado por Benson et al. (2012) encontró que era un plesiosaurio basal no neoplesiosaurio.

facts.statement: Anningasaura lived from the Hettangian to the Pliensbachian, between 201.4 and 184.2 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Hettangian to Pliensbachian (201.4 to 184.2 million years ago)
